questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I have been to Paris last year.
I have been to Paris three times.
questions.explanation: Present perfect ("have been") is used for life experience without a specific past time; "three times" fits, but "last year" needs the simple past.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the present perfect to talk about an unfinished period of time?
questions.explanation: "Since" + a point in time pairs with the present perfect to show an action continuing to the present.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: "We ___ (never/try) sushi before."
questions.explanation: "Have never tried" is the correct present perfect form for "we".

questions.question: Which sentence best emphasizes how long an action has been happening?
options: I read this book for a week.
I have read this book a week.
I've been reading this book for a week.
I am reading this book a week.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous highlights the duration of an ongoing activity.

questions.question: Complete: "It ___ raining since this morning."
questions.explanation: "Has been raining" (present perfect continuous) shows an action that started in the past and is still happening.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly describes an interrupted action in the past?
options: I watched TV when the power was going out.
I have watched TV when the power went out.
I am watching TV when the power went out.
I was watching TV when the power went out.
questions.explanation: Past continuous ("was watching") sets the background action interrupted by a simple past event ("went out").

questions.question: Complete: "At 8 p.m. last night, I ___ (do) my homework."
questions.explanation: Past continuous describes an action in progress at a specific past moment.

questions.question: Complete: "If you don't hurry, you ___ the train."
questions.explanation: First conditional: present simple in the "if" clause, "will" + base verb in the result clause.

questions.question: Which sentence is a correct first conditional?
options: If it rains, we will stay inside.
If it rains, we would stay inside.
If it will rain, we stay inside.
If it rained, we will stay inside.
questions.explanation: The "if" clause uses the present simple, and the result clause uses "will".

questions.question: Complete: "I'll help you if you ___ me first."
questions.explanation: In first conditional sentences, the "if" clause always takes the present simple.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses "as...as" to show equality?
options: This test is as more difficult as the last one.
This test is as difficulter as the last one.
This test is difficult as the last one.
This test is as difficult as the last one.
questions.explanation: The structure "as + adjective + as" uses the base form of the adjective, not the comparative.

questions.question: Complete: "My new phone isn't ___ my old one."
questions.explanation: "Not as + adjective + as" is used to show that one thing has less of a quality than another.

questions.question: Which modal verb best expresses a confident deduction, as in "The lights are on, so someone ___ be home"?
questions.explanation: "Must" expresses a strong, confident deduction based on evidence.

questions.question: Which sentence expresses a possibility, not a certainty?
options: She has been at the gym.
She must be at the gym.
She might be at the gym.
questions.explanation: "Might" expresses a possibility, while "must" expresses a strong deduction.

questions.question: Complete: "He ___ be the new manager — he doesn't have an office or a badge yet."
questions.explanation: "Can't" expresses a confident negative deduction, the opposite of "must".

questions.question: Which relative pronoun correctly completes: "The book ___ I bought yesterday is fantastic"?
questions.explanation: "That" (or "which") refers to things, so it correctly introduces a clause about a book.

questions.question: Which relative pronoun refers to a place?
questions.explanation: "Where" introduces a relative clause that describes a location.

questions.question: In the sentence "She had to put off the meeting until Friday," what does "put off" mean?
questions.explanation: "Put off" means to delay or postpone something to a later time.

questions.question: What does the phrasal verb "run into" mean in "I ran into an old friend at the mall"?
questions.explanation: "Run into" means to meet someone unexpectedly.

questions.question: What does "come across" mean in "I came across an interesting article yesterday"?
questions.explanation: "Come across" means to find or encounter something unexpectedly.

questions.question: Which sentence is in the simple present passive?
options: The reports are checked every morning.
The reports were checked every morning.
The reports have checked every morning.
questions.explanation: Simple present passive uses "am/is/are + past participle"; here it's "are checked".

questions.question: Complete: "This product ___ in three different colors."
questions.explanation: The passive form "is made" is used because the product doesn't perform the action itself.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the simple past passive?
options: The window broke was during the storm.
The window has broken during the storm.
The window is broken during the storm.
The window was broken during the storm.
questions.explanation: Simple past passive is formed with "was/were + past participle".

questions.question: Complete: "The email ___ by mistake yesterday."
questions.explanation: "Was deleted" is the simple past passive, used because the focus is on the email, not who deleted it.

questions.question: Tom said, "I am busy today." How is this reported?
options: Tom said he has been busy today.
Tom said he was busy that day.
Tom said he is busy today.
Tom said he will be busy today.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, present tense usually shifts to past, and "today" often changes to "that day".

questions.question: Maria said, "I will call you tomorrow." How is this reported?
options: Maria said she will call me tomorrow.
Maria said she is calling me tomorrow.
Maria said she would call me the next day.
Maria said she calls me tomorrow.
questions.explanation: "Will" in direct speech usually becomes "would" in reported speech.

questions.question: Complete: "I look forward to ___ you soon."
questions.explanation: The expression "look forward to" is followed by a gerund (-ing form).

questions.question: Complete: "She decided ___ a new language this year."
questions.explanation: The verb "decide" is followed by a "to" infinitive.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the past perfect?
options: When I arrived, she was already leaving.
When I arrived, she already left.
When I arrived, she had already left.
When I arrived, she has already left.
questions.explanation: Past perfect ("had already left") shows an action completed before another past action ("arrived").

questions.question: Complete: "By the time the firefighters arrived, the fire ___ most of the building."
questions.explanation: Past perfect shows the fire's destruction happened before the firefighters arrived.

questions.question: Which word describes food that has all the nutrients your body needs to stay healthy?
questions.explanation: "Nutritious" describes food that provides valuable nutrients for good health.

questions.question: Which word means to gradually recover your strength and health after an illness?
questions.explanation: "Recover" means to return to a normal, healthy state after being sick or injured.

questions.question: Which word refers to gases released into the air that cause pollution?
questions.explanation: "Emissions" are gases or particles released into the atmosphere, often causing pollution.

questions.question: Which word means the variety of plants and animals living in a particular area?
questions.explanation: "Biodiversity" refers to the range of different living species in an environment.

questions.question: Which word means to install the newest version of software on a device?
questions.explanation: "Update" means to install the latest version of an app or program.

questions.question: Which word describes a device or app that is no longer supported or useful?
questions.explanation: "Outdated" describes something old-fashioned that has been replaced by something newer.

questions.question: Which word describes a disagreement or argument between two people?
questions.explanation: "Conflict" refers to a disagreement or clash between people.

questions.question: Which word means to end a romantic relationship?
questions.explanation: "Break up" is a phrasal verb meaning to end a romantic relationship.

questions.question: Which word describes a person's list of qualifications, jobs, and experience, usually sent when applying for a job?
questions.explanation: A resume (or CV) summarizes a person's education, skills, and work experience.

questions.question: Which word means to officially leave your job?
questions.explanation: "Resign" means to formally announce that you are leaving a job.

questions.question: Which word refers to a detailed plan of a trip, including dates and places to visit?
questions.explanation: An "itinerary" is a planned schedule or route for a journey.

questions.question: Which word means a flight or trip that stops in another city before reaching the final destination?
questions.explanation: A "layover" is a stop between flights before continuing to the final destination.

questions.question: Which word describes someone who likes to plan things carefully and pays attention to detail?
questions.explanation: "Organized" describes someone who plans and manages things carefully.

questions.question: Which word describes someone who is willing to try new and different things?
questions.explanation: "Open-minded" describes a person willing to consider new ideas and experiences.

questions.question: Which word describes the feeling of being extremely happy and excited?
questions.explanation: "Thrilled" describes intense excitement and happiness.

questions.question: Which word describes feeling sad because you miss someone or something from the past?
questions.explanation: "Nostalgic" describes a sentimental longing for the past.

questions.question: Which word describes a group of people living in the same area who share resources and support each other?
questions.explanation: A "community" is a group of people living in the same area, often sharing common interests.

questions.question: Which word means the act of giving money or time to help people in need?
questions.explanation: "Charity" refers to helping people in need, often through donations.

questions.question: Which word describes a long period without rain that causes water shortages?
questions.explanation: A "drought" is an extended period of low rainfall leading to water shortages.

questions.question: Which word describes small ice crystals that form on surfaces on very cold mornings?
questions.explanation: "Frost" refers to the thin layer of ice that forms on cold surfaces.
